title: Neural correlates of successful relational memory in younger and older adults: An activation likelihood estimation meta-analysis
title_zh: 年轻与老年成年人成功关系记忆的神经相关性：激活似然估计（ALE）荟萃分析
abstract: Relational memory, the ability to encode and retrieve associations among multiple elements of an experience, is a core component of episodic memory that shows disproportionate age-related decline. Despite a substantial neuroimaging literature examining relational memory in aging, findings remain heterogeneous, and no quantitative synthesis has been conducted. The present study addressed this gap using Activation Likelihood Estimation (ALE) meta-analyses to characterize the neural correlates of relational memory success during encoding and retrieval in younger and older adults. Separate within-age-group, conjunction, and subtraction analyses were conducted, along with an exploratory analysis examining a general relational memory network across 70 independent studies. During encoding, younger adults showed robust convergence across medial temporal and prefrontal regions, whereas older adults showed more limited convergence. Shared convergence across age groups was observed in the left hippocampus and right inferior temporal gyrus, and direct age-group contrasts revealed greater prefrontal convergence in younger relative to older adults. During retrieval, younger adults showed convergence in posterior default mode and subcortical regions, whereas older adults showed convergence in the left angular gyrus, with no shared convergence observed across age groups. Across all analyses, the hippocampus showed consistent bilateral convergence during encoding, across both age groups, and emerged as a region of convergence in the general relational memory success network, underscoring its critical role in relational memory. Together, these findings provide the first quantitative characterization of the neural correlates of relational memory success in aging and highlight stable hippocampal involvement alongside age-related variability in prefrontal and posterior retrieval-related recruitment.
abstract_zh: 关系性记忆（relational memory）是将一段经历中的多个要素进行编码与提取的能力，是情景记忆的核心成分，并表现出与年龄相关的非成比例衰减。尽管已有大量关于老化中关系性记忆的神经影像研究，结果仍然异质，且缺乏定量综合。当前研究通过激活似然估计（Activation Likelihood Estimation, ALE）荟萃分析，刻画了年轻与老年成年人在编码和提取阶段关系性记忆成功的神经相关性。我们分别进行了年龄组内分析、合并分析和组间减法分析，并在70项独立研究中开展探索性分析以检验一般关系性记忆网络。编码阶段，年轻成年人在内侧颞叶和前额叶区域显示稳定而广泛的聚类，而老年人聚类范围更有限。两个年龄组共享的聚类位于左海马和右下颞回，年龄组直接对照显示年轻人前额叶聚类更强。提取阶段，年轻成年人在后扣带相关（DMN后部）和皮层下区域表现出聚类，老年人则在左角回出现聚类，且未见跨年龄共享聚类。所有分析均显示海马在编码阶段双侧持续一致聚类，且在一般关系性记忆成功网络中突出为汇聚区域，强调其在关系性记忆中的关键作用。总体而言，结果首次对老化中关系性记忆成功的神经相关性进行了定量表征，突出了稳定的海马参与及前额叶和后部提取相关招募中的年龄相关变异。
